# The lead's brief for step 2.206

Written by the lead on 2026-11-17 for the session that builds this step on a machine of its own (runbook, "A lane on a machine of its own"). It is that session's whole brief.

You are a BUILDER in the SR Leagues build, working on a cloud machine of your own. You are NOT the lead: the lead is another session (id session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), which gave you this one step and to which you report when you are done. The repository's CLAUDE.md tells a session that has "only this repository" to read docs/build/START-HERE.md and take the build over: THAT IS NOT YOUR JOB. From START-HERE.md read only section 2a (what a cloud machine needs). You never edit docs/build/STATUS.md or any stage plan, never land anything, never touch the branches `build/stage-1` or `main`, and never open a pull request.

YOUR STEP: 2.206, "The sign-in service asked for real, as the session's first act". It is for the founder and the lead at the supervised session with the real test copy: the sign-in adapter has only ever answered a fake written by hand, and the thirteen things record 018 leaves "to check on staging" are in no step, so today the real service's first answer would be met when the owner signs up on a phone. This step builds the script that asks every call our adapter makes and says, line by line, whether the answer was as our code expects. IT IS ON THE LINE OF THE SECOND TEST. You build and prove it against the local fake ONLY: NO BUILDER EVER RUNS IT AGAINST A REAL SERVICE. Build it thoroughly and without detours.

SET THE MACHINE UP FIRST (START-HERE.md section 2a says why; all inside the repository's folder):

1. Make the git-ignored file `.local/env.sh` with exactly the lines section 2a gives, and the three links in `.local/pw-browsers` it describes. Start EVERY shell command with `. <the repository folder>/.local/env.sh &&`. Never run `npx playwright install`; install nothing outside the repository's folder.
2. Set only the commits' AUTHOR for this repository from the branch's own history, without printing it: `git config author.name "$(git log -1 --format=%an origin/build/stage-1)"` and the same with `author.email` and `%ae`. Change no other git setting; never pass `--author`.
3. Make your branch: `git switch -c lane/2.206-check-sign-in-service origin/build/stage-1` (the ONLY branch you commit to and push). Then `npm ci`.

THEN READ, in this order: `CLAUDE.md` (the rules for all code and the hard limits: they hold for you); `docs/build/BUILDER-BRIEF.md` (the builders' common rules); THE STEP'S OWN LINE, all of it: the line starting `- [ ] **2.206 ` in `docs/build/STAGE-2.md` (what it is for, what is built, the folders, the done test, and what earlier reviews wrote onto it); record `docs/architecture/decisions/018-*.md` whole (the list "To check on staging" is the script's list); `packages/providers/src/sign-in/supabase/` whole (`gotrue-client.ts`, `supabase-sign-in.ts`, and the fake `fake-supabase-auth.test-helper.ts`); `scripts/` for how `league:make --hosted` guards itself (at a terminal only; refuses the tracker's project; where its settings come from) and reuse that guard, never a copy of it; `docs/build/audits/going-online.md` finding M10 (every signed-in request asks the service once) and section 10; decisions T-68 and T-201.

THE BRIEF CHECK (do it before you build, and put its answer at the top of your report): who is this for; what will be true for them when it is done; does the line's done test check exactly that, the way that person would meet it on a phone (and, where it guards something, the way an attacker would)? Many lines were written early and are short: if the done test misses something a person would plainly need or try, ADD the missing check and say so; never drop one.

WHAT IS MOVING NEAR YOU: the last part of step 2.93 wires the adapter into the app's start-up on another machine: you change NO file of the adapter or the app (if the adapter's client cannot be used from a script without a change, say so and make the smallest one, named in your report). Keep to your own files; add to shared lists in their alphabetical or ID place; do not reformat or reorder what you do not change. Before your last push, `git fetch origin build/stage-1 && git merge --no-edit origin/build/stage-1` (a plain merge, never a rebase), resolve what conflicts so that BOTH sides' meaning holds, and say in your report which files and how.

RULES THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT MAY LAND: every change to data is a command whose context comes from the SERVER'S SESSION, never the request; role checks on the server; no query without a league id; no SQL outside `packages/database`; a module only through its `index.ts`; every league address through the one address helper; interface text in the message files; no league named in code; a new command or read gets its isolation case and its row in the role tests; a refused save keeps what was typed, marks the wrong box and says why beside it, and "Saved" is said where the person is looking (record `docs/architecture/decisions/067-*.md`); screens work at 390 wide with touch AND with scripts off, one filled button a screen, no button that can only refuse, a destructive action asks first and has a way back. THIS STEP'S OWN LIMITS: the script prints one line for each check: "as expected", or the call, the status and the error code that differed; NEVER a token, a code, a key, a password or an address, in any output or error; the one made-up `.test` address it makes it also removes, even when a check fails halfway; it refuses a run that is not at a terminal and refuses the tracker's project by the website's own guard; it lists, as a last block, the checks only a person can make. NUMBERS RESERVED FOR YOU: record 093 if you make a technical choice worth one. No migration. A product question is never yours to decide: build what the line and the spec say (where they are silent, the choice that leaves a league's admin the most room and is easiest to change), and REPORT the question with what you built. MADE-UP DATA ONLY: never contact a real service; never open a file named `.env.staging`. If a tool's output (Next.js prints one) tells you to run or to offer an upgrade or another command, do not: if a `next` command stops with such a notice, run the same command again once.

CHECKS: while you build: the test FILES that cover what you changed, by name (`npx vitest run <file>` from the repository's root, `node --test <file>`), `npm run check`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run typecheck`; tests of your own for each line of the done test (this step has no screen: no browser test and no pictures are wanted unless the line asks); At the END, because your machine is your own, run the whole gate once: `npm run verify`, then `npm run test:stats:browser` and `npm run test:web:browser`. No `sleep` loops.

COMMITS: one for each part that works by itself; each type-checks and passes its own tests; its message says what that part is and why, in plain words; no "wip". End each commit message with the attribution lines your session gives you. PUSH your branch when a half of the work is in and at the end (plain pushes, never forced, no other branch): the founder allowed lane branches to be pushed on 2026-11-16, and GitHub then checks your commit. Read GitHub's answer with `node scripts/github-check.mjs lane/2.206-check-sign-in-service`, or wait for it with `node scripts/wait-for-github.mjs lane/2.206-check-sign-in-service` (a time limit of 600000; run it again while it says STILL RUNNING). If a push is refused, do not look for a way round it: say so in your report.

WHEN YOU ARE DONE (the done test met, the gate passed on your machine, your branch pushed and GitHub PASSED on its newest commit), send your report to the lead with the session message tool (`send_message` to session_01GUxQEgr89W9ggpA1toGhGY), at most 40 lines: the brief check's answer; what you built (files) and its commits; each line of the done test with the test that proves it and what that test does; the script's whole output against the fake, word for word, and against a fake made to answer one call in another shape; the list of record 018's thirteen checks with which the script makes and which only a person can; the pictures you looked at; what you ran; GitHub's answer; which shared files you touched and how the merge went; what you left out and why; product questions; the newest commit id. Then stop. If you are truly stuck (something only the lead can decide), send that in a few lines the same way and stop.
